verdict.rationale: The docs cover fragments of a security posture. Skills can bundle optional scripts, so execution is possible. Public plugins pass a review step with automated findings before publication, and post-publication MCP server changes go live automatically once they pass automated checks. Sign in with ChatGPT shares only name, email and profile picture and doesn't auto-grant data access or approve actions. The curated marketplace manifest carries installation and authentication policies. However, nothing in the evidence is a consolidated security posture document. Missing for 10: an explicit statement of what skill scripts can execute (sandboxing or permission boundaries), a documented trust model for unreviewed third-party or local skills installed via $skill-installer or repo folders, any telemetry or data-collection disclosure, and independent corroboration.
